mechanism_narrative: Persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in retail sales (RSAFS) and employment (PAYEMS) indicates robust consumer spending and income growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through higher corporate revenues.
failure_condition: The joint signal of RSAFS and PAYEMS both rising fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During low inflation periods (CPIAUCSL < 2.0% annualized), a decline in the federal funds rate accelerates monetary easing transmission to the real economy, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In low inflation periods (CPIAUCSL < 2.0%), the signal fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC is negative.

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing market activity (HOUST above 900,000 units) indicates robust consumer confidence and economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST exceeds 900,000, or Rank IC falls below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production exceeding 0.5% signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls > 0.5pp, or Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in federal funds rate and inflation above 2.5% annualized indicates policy response to inflation, triggering temporary market correction and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of FEDFUNDS declining and CPIAUCSL rising above 2.5% fails to produce negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC is above 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of labor market tightness (UNRATE < 6.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly), overheating risks increase monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: labor market tightness (UNRATE < 6.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5%)
failure_condition: In the specified labor market tightness regime, S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of cases over 20 days, or Rank IC for the regime is below 0.03.
